seo.title: PostgreSQL client for {devices}
seo.description: Connect to PostgreSQL with SSH, SSL/TLS, AWS IAM or ~/.pgpass, and to CockroachDB and PGlite on the same driver. EXPLAIN diagrams and pg_dump backups.

header.title: PostgreSQL client
header.lead: Query PostgreSQL, browse schemas and edit rows, and read EXPLAIN plans, jsonb, arrays and PostGIS values.

bands.title: Connect
text: Enter a host, port, user and database, or paste a postgresql:// or postgres:// URL; the database is required. New connections start with SSL set to Preferred, libpq’s sslmode=prefer. Choose Verify CA or Verify Identity to check the server’s certificate.

Use ~/.pgpass reads the password from ~/.pgpass and reports a file whose permissions would make libpq ignore it. Amazon RDS and Aurora sign in with AWS IAM for roles granted rds_iam, and Google Cloud SQL uses the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy. Connection Options takes anything libpq accepts, such as -c application_name=reporting.

bands.title: Query and edit
text: View <explain>EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE</explain> as diagrams or trees, and compare the plans of two runs. jsonb is formatted, array elements edit as a list, and enum columns offer their labels.

PostGIS geometry and geography values read as EWKT with their SRID, and a result with geometry opens on the <results>Map view</results>. A materialized view’s rows are read-only: refresh it from its menu, concurrently when the view has the unique index PostgreSQL requires.

bands.title: Schemas and structure
text: Create or edit a schema with its owner, comment and grants, and review the SQL first. Browse partition bounds and PostgreSQL Types: enums, composites, domains and ranges. Enum labels can be added or renamed.

A view’s definition is rebuilt with every table schema-qualified, and an index left invalid by a failed concurrent build is named in the Indexes tab. <compareSync>Compare & Sync</compareSync> ({compareSyncTier}) compares PostgreSQL schemas or data and holds back changes that could remove data.

bands.title: Administer
text: Users & Roles shows where each privilege comes from. The Server Dashboard shows sessions, cache hit ratio, database size and slow queries, and cancels a query with pg_cancel_backend or ends a session with pg_terminate_backend. A role that is neither a superuser nor a member of pg_monitor sees other sessions without their queries.

Preview VACUUM, ANALYZE, REINDEX and CLUSTER before they run. <backup>Backup Dump and Restore Dump</backup> run your own {dumpTool} and pg_restore through the connection’s SSH tunnel; for a PostgreSQL 9.1 server, use pg_dump 14 or earlier.

family.title: CockroachDB
text: CockroachDB uses the PostgreSQL driver that comes with the app, and new clusters start with the defaultdb database. For CockroachDB Cloud, copy the host, user, password and database from the Cloud console, put --cluster=your-cluster in Connection Options and set SSL Mode to Verify Identity; a local insecure node uses Disabled.
DDL comes from CockroachDB’s own SHOW CREATE, EXPLAIN text plans are parsed into the plan tree, and the Server Dashboard lists sessions and active queries. Foreign key checks cannot be deferred.

family.title: PGlite
text: PGlite is PostgreSQL compiled to WebAssembly. Start its socket server with npx @electric-sql/pglite-socket, adding --db=./my-pgdata to keep the data on disk, then connect to 127.0.0.1 rather than localhost. The server checks no password and has no TLS, so the form asks for neither.
Its catalogs are complete, so structure editing, Users & Roles and the EXPLAIN diagrams work as on a server, on its one database, postgres.

moveData: <importData>Import</importData> {importFormats} files, and export tables or results as {exportFormats}; SQL exports keep table, view and materialized-view comments. <copy>Copy To</copy> moves tables and their data to another PostgreSQL connection or another engine.
iphone: Switch databases and schemas from the toolbar, browse tables as cards, edit rows that have a primary key and run SQL in the Query tab. SSL runs from Required to Verify Identity, and SSH tunnels sign in with a password or a key.

faq.question: Does TablePro work with hosted PostgreSQL, such as Amazon RDS, Neon or Supabase?
faq.answer: Yes. A hosted server is a host and a port like any other, and Neon, Supabase and Heroku connect with the host they give you. They require TLS, which a new connection tries first.

faq.question: Can I reorder columns?
faq.answer: TablePro writes the script that rebuilds the table in the new column order and shows it to you, but never runs it. Run it yourself when the table can be rewritten.

otherTools.text: pgAdmin centers on PostgreSQL administration and Postico 2 on browsing and editing PostgreSQL on Mac; see <pgadmin>TablePro vs pgAdmin</pgadmin> and <postico>TablePro vs Postico 2</postico>.
